title: Intermittent electromagnetic compatibility exceedance after a packaging-driven routing change
engineering_question: A compliance test fails intermittently. What explains the intermittency, and what is the compliance exposure?
one_liner: A compliance measurement fails intermittently. Investigate.
initial_input: Full vehicle electromagnetic compatibility measurement shows an intermittent exceedance in one frequency band during DC charging. The exceedance is not reproducible on every run.
expected_impacted_domains: High voltage harness shielding and routing
expected_reasoning_paths: TR-012 and TR-013 both localise to the section re-routed by ECR-007, which converts a diffuse EMC problem into a specific design change consequence
Intermittency is explained by build-to-build routing variation - FM-240 is a process failure mode, not a design one
DOC-009 already recorded that EMC re-verification was required, so the process gap is that the required re-verification was not completed before the measurement
REQ-093 is still only in_review, which means the routing rule itself was not yet baselined when the change was implemented
known_unknowns: Per-vehicle routing records for the EMC test vehicles are not in the environment
Shield termination resistance history across builds is not available
Immunity margin after the routing change has not been measured
data_classification: SIMULATED ENTERPRISE ARTEFACT - not OEM, customer or proprietary data
